results.content:
Title: Explainable AI Improves Breast MRI Cancer Detection
Medical illustration highlighting breast abnormalities, illustrating diagnostic imaging and breast cancer detection. Clinician performing an abdominal ultrasound examination, illustrating non-invasive imaging for diagnostic assessment and routine clinical evaluation in patient care. # Explainable AI Improves Breast MRI Cancer Detection. Breast MRI scan showing detailed tissue structure for cancer detection and diagnosis. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers high sensitivity in detecting breast cancer, especially among women at elevated risk. A fully convolutional data description (FCDD) anomaly detection model has been developed to address these challenges, aiming to improve accuracy and explainability in both high- and low-prevalence breast MRI screening contexts. Most prior AI models for breast MRI have been evaluated using balanced datasets that do not reflect real-world prevalence, where malignant findings are rare. Anomaly detection offers a different approach by focusing on learning the characteristics of normal breast MRI scans, enabling better identification of abnormalities even when malignant cases are scarce. The FCDD model applies this principle to dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI data, generating pixel-level anomaly scores that can be aggregated into breast-level predictions. The model was developed using 9567 MRI examinations from 5026 patients collected over a decade, with two defined detection tasks: a balanced scenario including all cases and an imbalanced scenario reflecting realistic cancer prevalence. Imaging was processed into maximum intensity projections (MIPs), separated by breast and analysed using the FCDD model alongside comparison models, including binary cross-entropy (BCE) classification and hypersphere classification (HSC). Across both balanced and imbalanced detection tasks, FCDD consistently outperformed BCE in AUC and AUPR, while HSC showed similar performance to FCDD in some scenarios. In scenarios with realistic cancer prevalence, FCDD’s higher PPV and reduced false positives could translate to fewer unnecessary follow-ups, lowering patient anxiety and healthcare costs. The fully convolutional data description anomaly detection model represents a significant step forward in breast MRI screening, addressing both the performance drop seen in low-prevalence settings and the interpretability gap of prior AI approaches. While further validation in larger, lesion-annotated datasets and prospective clinical trials is needed, the model shows promise for enhancing breast MRI workflows, reducing false positives and improving diagnostic confidence.

results.title: MRI, CT, and AI: How Technology is Improving Medical Imaging - MIDTOWN MEDICAL IMAGING
results.content: # MRI, CT, and AI: How Technology is Improving Medical Imaging From faster scan analysis to more precise diagnoses, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the game in modern medicine, especially in the world of imaging. Today, AI medical imaging tools are helping radiologists detect abnormalities earlier, reduce interpretation errors, and improve patient outcomes across modalities like MRI, CT, and ultrasound. ## The Basics of AI in Diagnostics Artificial intelligence in imaging refers to software that can “learn” from data, analyzing patterns, highlighting abnormalities, and even predicting outcomes based on thousands of cases. ### Key Benefits of AI Diagnostics * Early detection of conditions like tumors, fractures, or infections * Fewer false positives and negatives * Automated comparisons with previous scans for tracking changes * Faster report generation, improving turnaround times Whether you’re coming in for an MRI, CT scan, or ultrasound, AI algorithms assist radiologists by identifying areas of concern, flagging unusual patterns, and helping prioritize urgent cases. ## AI Across Imaging Modalities: MRI, CT, Ultrasound AI isn’t limited to one type of imaging—it’s enhancing accuracy across the board. ### MRI AI With high-resolution imaging and vast data, MRI AI tools help identify brain lesions, joint issues, or spinal abnormalities with improved clarity and speed. ## Real-World Applications and Results At Midtown Medical Imaging, we’re already seeing the benefits of AI-assisted diagnostics: * Faster scan review times mean shorter patient wait times * Higher confidence in complex case interpretation * Better consistency across patient follow-ups By combining AI support with the expertise of our board-certified radiologists, we’re delivering more precise and timely results for every patient. Researchers are developing tools that can: * Customize treatment plans based on imaging data * Integrate with electronic medical records for full-picture analysis As these tools evolve, Midtown Medical Imaging remains committed to adopting safe, effective AI enhancements to serve our community with excellence. Midtown Medical Imaging stays ahead of the curve by integrating advanced AI healthcare tech into our diagnostic services. #### One Of A Kind Midtown Medical Imaging is currently the only outpatient imaging center in the region to offer this advanced diagnostic system.
